Description: Home to Humpback Rocks, one of the most popular destinations along the Blue Ridge Parkway at milepost 5.8. From the summit, visitors can see into the southern section of Shenandoah National Park to the north, a patchwork of farms to the east, and the thick woods and mountain ridges of the George Washington National Forest to the southwest. The granite outcrop at Humpback Rocks offers Virginia's premier traditional climbing routes, with clean, solid granite featuring classic Blue Ridge routes that demand both technical skill and mental fortitude. Description: Historic community featuring Woodson's Mill, a water-powered grist mill built in 1794 by Guiliford Campbell. The original four-story, 32-foot square structure has been owned and maintained by several families over the years, with the Fulcher family adding two millstones in the 1840s that are still operational today. Dr. Julian B. Woodson expanded the mill in the early 20th century, incorporating an icehouse, sawmill, and foundry. After restoration in the early 1980s, the mill continues to produce stone-ground grain products. Deep Roots Milling operates at the mill one Sunday each month, offering a variety of flours and meals made from regionally grown grains. Adjacent to the mill is the Woodson's Mill House, a Craftsman-style home available for lodging, providing visitors an opportunity to stay near this historic landmark.
